title: The existence of symmetric cyclic Steiner quadruple systems
summary: A Steiner quadruple system of order $v$, denoted by $\operatorname{SQS}(v)$, is called cyclic if it admits $\mathbb Z_v$ as a group of automorphisms acting regularly on its point set. A cyclic system is called symmetric cyclic, or S-cyclic, if the multiplier $-1$ preserves each block orbit individually. Grannell and Griggs conjectured in 1983 that such a system of order $v$ exists if and only if $v\equiv2,4,10,20\pmod{24}$ and every odd prime divisor $p$ of $v$ satisfies $p\equiv1$ or $5\pmod{12}$.
